$comment: Winter trench scene on the Eastern Front; place and date are as described by the supplier and are not established by an archive record — see notes.

original.description: German infantry resting in a snow-covered trench cut into pale soil. Most wear the M1907/10 greatcoat and the Pickelhaube under a cloth cover; one man on the parapet keeps watch with his rifle, another stands at the right in marching order with pack, rolled greatcoat, mess tin and bayonet, a scarf wound to his ears. Others sit or lie along the trench floor and against the wall, one asleep at the foot of the frame. Rifles lie along the parapet; a dugout entrance opens behind the seated men.
original.date: described as 1914; on internal evidence the winter of 1914–15
original.archive: no archive of record — supplied without a source, and no holding institution has been traced for it
original.licence: public domain — a German photograph of the First World War, published well before 1931

content_policy: ok — men resting and on watch; the figure at the foot of the frame is asleep, and no casualties are shown
caption: German infantry resting in a snow-filled trench on the Eastern Front, winter 1914–15 — greatcoats, covered Pickelhauben, and one man still watching the parapet. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: photographer not identified, German army, winter 1914–15; public domain. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Supplied by Dave 2026-08-23 as 'German soldiers resting after a battle in East Prussia in 1914'. PROVENANCE IS THE WEAKEST OF THIS BATCH and the caption is written accordingly: no source was supplied, and searching did not trace a holding archive, so neither the place nor the engagement can be stated. What the image itself supports is the season and the army — deep snow with covered Pickelhauben and M1907/10 greatcoats puts it in the winter of 1914–15, before the Stahlhelm — so the caption says 'the Eastern Front, winter 1914–15' rather than naming East Prussia or a battle. Note that the same kit and snow would fit the Vosges, the Argonne or the Carpathians equally well. For the image review (sand-y0u.7): trace an archive copy, or replace it. Natural placement if it can be sourced: the Tannenberg eastern cross-reference (1914:tannenberg-east, shipped in PR #68) and the winter that followed it.
